legs.note: PORTED FROM BONNIE, RE-IMPLEMENTED ON MARY'S PRIMITIVES. When a navigation lands on a human-check interstitial (recognised from the shell title Mary already reads, no scripted poll), the engine presses the visible 'verify you are human' checkbox ONCE through the same HID click the rest of the page lane uses — the real cursor a person moves — and looks again. It does not forge a token, spoof a fingerprint, or use a solver: it operates the visible control on the person's own screen, and if one press does not clear it, refuses humanCheck ("could you click it?") rather than hammering. The contract is pinned by PageChallengeTests with fakes; this leg waits on a real challenge page to record against, which cannot be staged deterministically.
legs.say: go to a site that checks you're human first

summary: A page behind a 'verify you are human' check is entered by pressing its checkbox, or handed back honestly.
